pages.text: Each fission frees neutrons; k = η f p ε of them cause the next fission, less what leaks out and what the control rods absorb. The salt expands as it warms and k falls by 4 pcm per kelvin, so the reactor settles at the temperature where k is exactly 1. Pumping the salt through the heat exchanger carries that heat to the turbine.
$(thing)Set$(): Fuel concentration, Control rod insertion, Salt flow.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Xenon and burn-up: reactivity drifts by ±0.2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The fuel salt is freezing (below 732 K): the freeze plug has drained the core; Above 980 K the Hastelloy-N vessel creeps; Prompt critical: reactivity above the delayed-neutron fraction; No salt flow: the heat has nowhere to go.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Power output follows the electric power.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Thermal utilisation f: f = Σ_fuel/(Σ_fuel + Σ_other)$(br)k∞: k∞ = η f p ε$(br)k at 900 K: k = k∞·P_NL·(1 − w·r)$(br)Reactivity: ρ = (k − 1)/k$(br)Salt temperature: T = 900 K + ρ/α_T$(br)Thermal power: P = Q·c_p·(T − T_return)$(br)Cycle efficiency: η = 0.65·(1 − T_cold/T)
